summary: Carney and Trump met for about 20 minutes at APEC and agreed to keep talking, with no deal yet; Canada and China cut more tariffs, and inflation held at 3.1%.
body: Prime Minister Mark Carney and Donald Trump met for about 20 minutes on Wednesday in Shenzhen, just before the APEC leaders' dinner, with Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand and senior US trade officials in the room.[^1] Carney's office said they discussed a "mutually beneficial trade agreement", and Carney wrote that they "agreed to continue the work and to stay in close contact".[^1][^2] No deal or tariff change was announced. The Canadian Press reports that the issues on the table included protections for French and a viable Canadian auto sector, the same points that stalled talks in August. Anand said Canada will keep spreading its trade to other countries whatever happens in the US midterm elections.[^3]

A day earlier, Carney and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed to more tariff cuts. China will ease tariffs on about $400 million of Canadian exports such as frozen pork, fish and seafood, and Canada will extend exemptions on some Chinese steel and aluminum for two more years.[^1][^4] The federal government says the trip also finished free-trade talks with the Philippines and "substantially concluded" talks with ASEAN, a group of 10 Southeast Asian countries, with both deals to be signed in 2027. It estimates the ASEAN deal could add about 14,000 Canadian jobs; that is the government's own estimate.[^5]

At home, Statistics Canada said on Monday that inflation held at 3.1% in October. Gasoline cost 30.9% more than a year earlier, which Global News links to high oil prices during the war in Iran; without gasoline, prices rose 2%.[^6] In Ontario, Transportation Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria said the government is tabling a bill to raise the minimum fine for noisy vehicles from $60 to $200, saying loud vehicles can drown out emergency sirens.[^7] My read: apart from the summit, it was a fairly quiet day in Canadian and Ontario politics.
